I am 46 years old and have farmed this 3.5 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. My family has seven people, and my husband and older son work in a factory in Handan city, so they send some money home. That helps me buy inputs, but I still count every yuan because 3.5 mu is not much land. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the seed dealer tells me, but I trust what I see in my own field more than anything written in a book. I mostly do what worked last year and I watch my neighbors. If they use a new seed and their yield looks good, I will try it too.

For winter wheat, I plant right after National Day in early October. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu, so I will buy the same improved seed variety from the dealer in town. Before sowing, I run the rotary tiller to break up the maize stubble. I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as a base — that gives me about 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium. Then I topdress twice with urea, about 30 kg total per mu, which is another 14 kg of nitrogen. I irrigate three times from the well: once in late March when the wheat wakes up, once at jointing in April, and once at grain filling in May. I spray twice — once for weeds, and once for insects and fungus when the weather turns warm. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the spring frost does not hit.

For summer maize, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plough, so I seed directly into the wheat stubble — the stubble keeps the soil moist and saves me labor. I use hybrid seed, one small bag is enough. I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then add 25 kg of urea at the big-flare stage. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once around the 7-leaf stage if the rain does not come, and once when the ears are filling. I spray herbicide once when the seedlings are small, and insecticide once later if I see worms. I expect about 600 kg per mu. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield — on 3.5 mu, a bad harvest is a disaster for our family budget, but wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost I can absorb.
